: O R D E R :
MR. J.BAG, LD. MEMBER 

 

  

 

The present appeal is directed
against the Order dated 03.08.2011 passed by the Ld. District Consumer Disputes
Redressal Forum, Kolkata, Unit II in Case No. CDF/Unit-II/CC No. 1385 OF 2009
in the matter of Sri Samar Roychoudhury
-vs- Hotel New Sea Hawk, Marine Drive, Swargadwar, Puri 752001 and others.
The
facts relating to the case are as follows:
The Appellant / Complainant, a senior
citizen of 69 years and a legal practitioner at Honble Calcutta High Court,
decided to go to Puri on a pleasure trip in October 2009 and accordingly booked
an accommodation in the Respondent /OP 1s Hotel at Puri for 7 days from 1st to 7th October 2009 with the help of OP No. 2
located at 48/A, Dr. Sundari Mohan Avenue, Kolkata 700014 on payment of Rs.
15,750/-. The accommodation being Room
No. 201 or Room No. 301 of the OPs hotel at Puri was offered by the Respondent
No. 2 and recommended to be suitable for four heads at the enquiry of the
Complainant / Appellant . The said
accommodation was written as One A/C Suite Room No. 201 / 301 in voucher No
3290 dated 06.07.09 which was issued to
the Appellant /Complainant on the day of booking in advance . Having reached
the Hotel on 1st October 2009
the Appellant was allegedly shocked as the actual state of things in
regard to the A/C Suite Room No. 201/301 fell short of his expectation /understanding
about what a suite in particular should be like . He felt dissatisfied as the room
he was put in was a double bedded room only and was not suitable for accommodation
of four adult persons. The inconvenience was brought to the knowledge of the
managers of the hotel forthwith, but they expressed their inability to help the
Appellant/ Complainant as the booking was done from Kolkata office. The
Appellant wanted to leave the hotel on cancellation of the booking from the
next date and demanded refund of money after deduction of one days charges as
payable for their stay, but the OPs did not comply. He could arrange better
accommodation but, since the refund was refused, he with his family members
rather unwillingly had to stay put there in uncomfortable condition and that
was a deficiency in service on the part of the Respondents/ OPs. as alleged.
After returning from Puri the Appellant/ Complainant sent a letter on 12.10.2009 alleging about the
deficiency in service on the part of the Respondents / OPs particularly in regard
to the absence of facilities associated with a suite and non -refund of money
on cancellation of the booking for the
period from 2nd to 7th October 09, and also
claiming refund of the entire amount of Rs.15,750/- together with compensation
of a sum of Rs. 75, 000/-.
The OPs denied and disputed the
allegations in a reply letter issued by an Advocate on their behalf thereby
leading to the filing of a consumer complaint case which was admitted and
registered by the Ld. District Forum below for adjudication. The Learned
District Forum after having gone through the complaint and other documents and
evidences dismissed the complaint observing that no assurance was given to the
complainant that the suite will be having an ante room as the Appellant /
Complainant pleaded for in his complaint inter alia . The Ld. District Forum
below also did not find any evidence as to the uncomfortable conditions which
the Respondent /Complainant alleged to have experienced during their stay at
the OPs Hotel. As such, the Complainant has been, vide order of the Ld.
District Forum, directed to pay Rs. 5000/- (Rupees five thousand only) to the
O.P No. 1 as cost for falsely alleging deficiency of service against it.
Being
aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order of the Ld. District Forum the Appellant
/Complainant preferred an Appeal stating
all facts and praying for orders so that the impugned judgment of the
Ld. District Forum is set aside and operation and / or execution of the
impugned judgment is stayed .
We
have gone trough the Appeal together with other documents, evidences, written
submissions including BNA of the Appellant, Written Argument of the contesting
Respondents/OPs and the impugned judgment, apart from the case judgment of the
Honble National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission reported under V (2010)
CPJ65 (NC). The LCR being called for has
been perused along with Xerox copy of Page 770 of the Oxford Dictionary containing the meaning
etc. of the word suite. We heard both
parties and then decided to make an order .
Decision with Reasons :
The Appellant / Complainant visited
the Booking Office of the Respondent No. 1 at 48/A Dr. Sundari Mohan Avenue , Kolkata on 6th July 2009 and talked to the
Respondent No. 2 who showed some brochures containing pictures, rooms, tariff
and facilities of the Hotel of the
Respondent No. 1 at Puri. He booked an accommodation described / written as 
One A/c Suite Room No. 201 or 301 for October 1 7, 2009 for a total payment
of Rs. 15750 /-. But when on 01.10.2009 he reached the Hotel with other members
of his family and checked in, he was shocked to see that though it was Room No. 201 as shown in the booking
voucher it was anything but a suite. He felt dissatisfied and inconvenienced.
Managers of the Hotel had no other alternative than to make him stay in that
room and the Appellant / Complainant in
a bid to leave the said accommodation the very next day claimed refund of such
amount as would have been payable after deducting the charges for one days
stay. That was refused. The Appellant / Complainant therefore stayed in the Hotel for the entire
period as booked and later made it to the Ld. District Consumer Disputes
Redressal Forum urging for reliefs i.e.Refund of Rs. 15750/- with interest @
12%, a sum of Rs. 75000/- for harassment and mental agony and Rs. 7500/-as litigation costs.
We have gone through the Appeal, BNAs,
Judgment of the Ld. District Forum and case references as in IV (2010) CPJ
65(NC ) and other documents as placed before us.
It appears from voucher No. 3290 dated
06. 07. 09 that Room No. 201 which was
during his stay at the Hotel occupied by the Appellant was described /shown /
written as A/C Suite Room at the time of
booking .
In dismissing the complaint the Ld.
District Forum observed inter alia that no assurance was given to the
complainant the suite will be having an ante room. It may be true that there
was no such assurance on the part of the booking personnel, but describing / writing or showing the room in the booking voucher (issued by an authorised person of
the Respondent No.1) as a suite is either a lapse or a motivated act in the
nature of a deceitful ploy to attract customers, simply
because a suite to be a suite must have at least two rooms, whatever their size
or facilities and a hotelier is more
conversant with what a suite exactly means than a man in the street or an ordinary
guest availing a hotel room. Describing a particular room as suite and booking it
as such definitely arouses an expectation about better facilities than in case
of a room only on the part of the hirer and the offerer is bound to make sure that he offered a suite and not one
room. That the said act of the person in charge of booking was a lapse,
intentional or otherwise, has never been admitted in course of hearing of the
complaint or the Appeal. There is strong reason to believe that the Respondent
No1 has been indulging in such deceptive practice which is nothing but an
unfair trade practice. The Appellant has brought to light the deficiency in
service on the part of the Respondents/OPs.
He has proved his point.
In view of what has been stated it is ORDERED that-
The appeal succeeds on contest and
the impugned judgment is set aside. The Respondent shall refund a sum of
Rs.7325/- being 50% of the total payment made towards accommodation charges,
Rs.10000/- as compensation for harassment and mental agony, apart from Rs.
3000/- as litigation charges within 45 days from the date of this order failing
which interest @ 8% on such sums shall be payable to the Appellant till
realization in full.
